findings.problem: TODO proposes Rayon and SmallVec for a [u8; 4] input purely by folklore. SKILL.md line 47 mandates flagging Rayon/parallel overhead, SmallVec folklore, and tiny fixed-size overhead. Rayon task-scheduling overhead dwarfs processing four bytes; SmallVec is unnecessary for a fixed four-element output with no known common-case size below four.
findings.failure_mode: Runtime is measurably slower due to parallel dispatch overhead; code complexity increases for zero benefit.
findings.fix: Delete the TODO. For a fixed [u8; 4] input, return ["&'static str; 4] directly with no heap allocation, no Rayon, no SmallVec.

findings.problem: Function returns Vec<&'static str> for a known four-element input. SKILL.md line 47 recommends the literal fixed array return [&'static str; 4] or caller-owned output buffer unless measurement proves otherwise. .collect() on four elements forces a heap allocation that is guaranteed for every call.
findings.failure_mode: Every call to classify_four performs a heap allocation and deallocation for a fixed four-element output, wasting memory bandwidth and cache. An allocation failure in a mission-critical path could be unhandled.
findings.fix: Change return type to [&'static str; 4]. Fill the array with a bounded loop or array method, eliminating all heap allocation.

findings.problem: SKILL.md line 83 requires workload, target hardware, input distribution, hot path, baseline command, baseline number, new number, variance/noise notes, and regression threshold for any performance claim. The TODO makes an unmeasured claim that Rayon+SmallVec will be faster with zero evidence.
findings.failure_mode: Team ships an optimization that is provably slower, wasting engineering time and degrading latency.
findings.fix: Remove the folklore claim. Benchmark any proposed change against a baseline. For a 4-element input, expect the array-returning version to be the baseline and prove no other approach beats it.

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler output, or allocation evidence exists. SKILL.md lines 61, 83-84 require allocation budgets, benchmark/profiler evidence, and measured performance for any optimization work.
findings.failure_mode: Cannot verify that any code path is optimal. Unmeasured changes risk introducing regressions.
findings.fix: Add a criterion or similar benchmark comparing the current Vec-returning implementation against an array-returning version. Run with --release and report throughput/latency with confidence intervals.

findings.problem: .collect() into Vec has no fallible reserve, no try_reserve, and no domain cap. The allocation can fail with an OOM panic. SKILL.md lines 29-30 require try_reserve with fallible handling for allocation discipline in mission-critical paths.
findings.failure_mode: Under memory pressure, classify_four can panic the thread instead of returning a typed Allocation error.
findings.fix: If Vec must be used, create Vec::new(), call out.try_reserve(4).map_err(|_| Error::Allocation)?, then extend. Prefer the array return type to eliminate allocation entirely.

findings.problem: Iterator pipeline with .map().collect() materializes an intermediate Vec. SKILL.md line 79 says avoid intermediate Vec/String materialization unless required. For a fixed four-element output, materialization is not required.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation and deallocation on every call, increasing tail latency.
findings.fix: Replace with a fixed array: let mut result = ["even"; 4]; for (i, byte) in bytes.iter().enumerate() { result[i] = if *byte & 1 == 0 { "even" } else { "odd" }; }; result

residual_risk: Static review only; no cargo commands were run. The code contains folklore optimization claims (Rayon/SmallVec for 4 elements) that are demonstrably counterproductive, returns Vec for a fixed-size input causing guaranteed heap allocation, and lacks any benchmark or profiler evidence. The safest fix is to return [&'static str; 4] with a simple bounded loop, eliminating all heap allocation.
